short: Britain's current tank, and the last in the world with a rifled main gun.
full:
Challenger 2 was a Vickers private venture rather than a government design, ordered in 1991 and taken into British Army service in June 1998; 386 were built. It shares little but a name with Challenger 1, using second-generation Dorchester composite armour, a new turret and fire-control system, and the 120 mm L30A1 rifled gun firing bagged charges. Britain kept rifling for the sake of HESH ammunition long after everyone else moved to smoothbores.

Its main campaign was Iraq in 2003, where it led the entry into Basra. One tank was destroyed by another Challenger in a friendly-fire incident; another absorbed a reported seventy RPG hits without a crew fatality. The first Challenger 2 lost to enemy action was one of fourteen given to Ukraine in 2023. Of the surviving fleet, 148 are being converted to Challenger 3 and the remainder will leave service, though the tank has also served with Oman.
